analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: FLIGHT TO SAFETY 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +33bps at 7,744 with a $5Bn MOC to sell. NDX -5bps at 29,935, R2K +134bps at 2,766, Dow +108bps at 52,177. Volume was 20.826bn shares vs a YTD daily average of 18.571bn.

The session was volatile. It opened with a Tech/AI sell-off after Korea fell 7% overnight. The GS desk saw more Long Only activity, with an early wave of supply in Semis around the open that slowed as the session went on.

A 'flight to safety' bid showed in pockets of Mag7, Staples, MedTech & Tools, and Financials. The mid-day drift higher was a broadening out with RTY > SPX > NDX. The desk saw no meaningful defense in AI or peripheral pockets.

Quoting Privo: the pain trade was long AI / short bonds, and both sides are now unwinding. Credit concerns have entered the AI spending equilibrium, and the market increasingly reads this as a growth shock.

Flows: the floor was 8/10 in the morning, with Long Onlys -40% better for sale. By the afternoon it was 6/10 with LOs -25% better for sale, driven by tech supply vs demand in financials and healthcare. Hedge funds were -3% better for sale, with small supply in tech, healthcare and consumer discretionary.

Callahan: risk appetite is not great, with risk-off price action and flows in a compressed calendar window into year-end. Unlike the July momentum unwind, which was mostly technical after the April-June run, this episode has more debate over which 'wall of worry' (earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation) is most acute.
NDX forward P/E is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023. The note suggests this could support earnings season.

Positioning: the GS sentiment indicator has been negative for 6 straight weeks, and the last reading was its lowest at -1.3. Overall length is not max long. The AI trade is still long but is now about 6/10 in length and cleaner than in June/July.
Yesterday was the 2nd largest net selling in the past year in the Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI).

Derivatives: a 'squeezy' tape as indices swung back off intraday lows. Skew opened offered and kept getting hit as spot stabilized. Fixed strike vols drifted lower, with gamma tenors offered most aggressively. RUT vol caught a bid in the belly and back end of the curve.

Options flow: clients tilted to sellers of skew after yesterday's heavy bid. In singles and thematic names, clients monetized hedges and defended positioning while rolling down strikes, particularly in MAG7.
The squeeze was visible in the High Beta 12m Losers (GSCBLMOM) and Liquid Most Short (GSXUMSAL) baskets, which topped the leaderboard.
Warsh is scheduled to speak at 11:30pm on 15 Oct. The S&P implied move through 16 Oct is 0.54%.

Oil rose 2.74% on the day, to just under $100.
This is the options-implied one-day move into the Warsh speech and the next session.

crypto_views: Bitcoin closed +72bps at $82,299. The note makes no crypto-specific argument.
